global_deviations.description: Docker toolchain. Base image nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu24.04; host and CUDA-host compiler clang-18 (never the distribution gcc); nvcc from /usr/local/cuda-12.8; CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release for every method; Ninja generator. Eigen pinned to 3.4.0. OpenCV pinned to 4.12.0 with opencv_contrib, built static with BUILD_LIST=core,imgcodecs,imgproc,calib3d,cudev,highgui,viz, WITH_CUDA=ON, WITH_VTK=ON. PCL comes from Ubuntu's libpcl-dev and is linked by HPM-MVS only. None of the eleven methods was released against this toolchain, so no measurement here is a measurement of the authors' binaries.

CUDA architecture target. Passed to every method build as -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<arch>. The campaign target is 120 (the Blackwell benchmark fleet); the local development GPU is 75. Every published number states which. `deviations verify --arch <arch> --image <image>` runs `cuobjdump -res-usage` on each built binary inside the image and requires the method's own kernels to carry SASS for exactly that architecture; the statically linked OpenCV CUDA modules (`cv::cudev::…`) ship SASS for sm_50–sm_120 regardless and are only checked for covering the target (D22). Upstream's ACMH, ACMM, ACMP, ACMMP, MP-MVS and DPE-MVS created their targets with FindCUDA's `cuda_add_executable`, which ignores CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES and CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS; every fork now builds through enable_language(CUDA) (one `build` commit each, see the forks' logs), so the flag is authoritative everywhere and the binary check is what keeps that claim honest over time.

Common nvcc flags. The ACM lineage ships `-O3 --use_fast_math --maxrregcount=128 --ptxas-options=-v` in CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS and the harness keeps them. --use_fast_math changes device floating-point semantics and --maxrregcount=128 is an occupancy control, so both are load-bearing for runtime and for the numbers. They must reach the actual compile path in every fork. The MP-MVS fork had moved them to CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS while its target was still created with `cuda_add_executable`, so it was compiled with neither (fork-audit.md § B.8 #3c, § C.1); repaired by its `build: build CUDA through the CUDA language` commit, verified on the nvcc command line and with cuobjdump. No MP-MVS number predates the repair.

In the `norm10` configuration one shared converter, `colmap2mvsnet_acm_perf`, replaces the shipped converter of every method and emits 10 source views instead of the shipped 20. View selection is byte-identical in all five shipped variants, so the substitution changes no neighbour ranking; it equalises the image bytes and intrinsics that variants D/E (APD-MVS, DVP-MVS, DPE-MVS) otherwise pad, re-encode and rescale. Applies to `norm10` only; `author` runs each fork's own converter (R-EXP-06). Padding under `norm10` is all-or-none per scene (R-EXP-09).

Debug artefact output disabled in every configuration behind a single `--no-debug-output` flag, with the upstream behaviour left as the binary's default. Upstream ships debug output ON in seven of the ten campaign methods: DPE-MVS's DEBUG_COMPLEX (a full-resolution D2H copy plus a JPEG encode per RunPatchMatch) and show_medium_result=true (3 JPEGs per image pass, plus 2 per edge pre-pass), APD-MVS's show_medium_result forced true in main (3 JPEGs per image pass), MP-MVS's four config.yaml switches plus an unconditional costs.jpg per image pass, HPM-MVS's depths_prior.dmb per prior pass, HPM-MVS++'s triangulation*.png and up to two depths_prior*.dmb per prior pass, and the triangulation.png of ACMP, ACMMP and MP-MVS. Every fork's default is the upstream behaviour, config.yaml and DPE's #define DEBUG_COMPLEX included; the flag only adds a way to skip the writes at run time. ACMH and ACMM write no debug artefacts and take no flag; CUMVS writes none unless -d is given and its OpenCV CommandLineParser rejects unknown keys, so the flag must NOT be passed to it. Per policy rule 1 both settings are measured in the pilot so the pair is a result, not just a disclosure.

Phase-timer instrumentation. A single `bench_timer.h` vendored byte-identically into all ten campaign forks (md5 must match across them), emitting `PHASE <name> BEGIN|END <monotonic_ns> [k=v ...]` for the canonical_phases above to the file named by MVS_BENCH_FILE, line buffered so a crashed or killed run keeps its partial trace. It is compiled out entirely under -DBENCH_PHASES=0 and, when compiled in, takes one cached always-false branch per boundary unless MVS_BENCH_PHASES is set; output never goes to the binary's own stdout or stderr. Every kernel launch in the nine non-CUMVS methods is already followed by cudaDeviceSynchronize, so every canonical phase boundary is a true sync point and no extra synchronisation is introduced. CUMVS has two unsynchronised launches (initializeDepthsAndNormals, calcInitialCosts); their cost is attributed to the following patchmatch.propagate span unless MVS_BENCH_SYNC is set, which inserts one cudaDeviceSynchronize at the end of patchmatch.init and must itself be measured as an on/off pair (R-TIM-08). Overhead must be measured (instrumented vs BENCH_PHASES=0 build), not assumed (R-TIM-09).
global_deviations.reversible: flag BENCH_PHASES=0 at compile time; env var at run time

global_deviations.description: Dataset presentation. The harness binds an ETH3D scene into the container as three read-only mounts: `images/`, `dslr_calibration_undistorted/`, and the same calibration directory a second time as `sparse/`. The ACM-lineage converters (ACMH, ACMM, ACMP, ACMMP, HPM-MVS, HPM-MVS++, MP-MVS) read `<dense_folder>/sparse` as a COLMAP dense workspace would have it; APD-MVS, DPE-MVS and CUMVS read `dslr_calibration_undistorted` directly. Both see identical bytes; no fork's converter is edited and nothing is copied or rewritten. Image paths in images.txt carry the `dslr_images_undistorted/` prefix, so `images/<name>` resolves for both.

fork_deviations.rationale: The released script cannot configure on the benchmark toolchain, and its hardcoded sm_30/sm_52 architectures do not cover the benchmark GPU. The GNUCXX-only block that added -ffast-math -march=native is disabled rather than deleted; it never fired under the clang-18 toolchain used here, so this is behaviour-neutral for this harness, but it is not behaviour-neutral in general.
fork_deviations.subject: build: modernise CMake and raise the language standard to C++20

fork_deviations.rationale: The benchmark image builds OpenCV with BUILD_LIST=core,imgcodecs,imgproc,calib3d,cudev,highgui,viz as static libraries. Requesting only the components ACMH actually uses keeps the link line and the resulting binary minimal, so that link-time differences between methods do not come from unused static libraries.
fork_deviations.subject: build: request only the OpenCV components ACMH uses

fork_deviations.rationale: Keeps build directories and editor state out of the fork so that the deviation verifier and `git log upstream-base..HEAD` see only real source deviations.
fork_deviations.subject: interface: ignore build output and editor state

fork_deviations.rationale: Targets created by `cuda_add_executable` are compiled by FindCUDA, which reads `CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS` and ignores both `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` and `CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS`. With the upstream -gencode list removed, nvcc therefore fell back to its built-in default architecture and the benchmark GPU ran JIT'd PTX rather than native SASS, while the forks that already used `enable_language(CUDA)` were built natively for sm_75. Comparing methods compiled two different ways is not defensible in a study about implementation overhead, so all forks are moved onto the same path and the architecture is supplied by the harness. The device C++ standard is pinned to the same value the fork already passed to nvcc.
fork_deviations.subject: build: build CUDA through the CUDA language so the target architecture is honoured

fork_deviations.rationale: `np.asscalar` was deprecated in NumPy 1.16 and removed in NumPy 1.23, so the shipped converter raises AttributeError on any NumPy the benchmark image can install. `ndarray.item()` is the documented replacement and returns the same Python scalar.
fork_deviations.subject: compat: replace np.asscalar with ndarray.item in the shipped converter

fork_deviations.rationale: ACMH hardcodes `cudaSetDevice(1)`, so it fails outright on a single-GPU machine and silently uses a different GPU than the rest of the family on a multi-GPU one. Device selection is the harness's job, done with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; every sibling in the ACM family already calls `cudaSetDevice(0)` (ACMM main.cpp:77, ACMP main.cpp:38, ACMMP main.cpp:77).
fork_deviations.subject: compat: select CUDA device 0 instead of device 1

fork_deviations.rationale: The harness needs a per-phase timing breakdown (SPEC R-TIM-01, R-TIM-04, R-TIM-05) that is comparable across all ten campaign methods, and ACMH ships no timers at all. A vendored header-only tracer keeps the measurement inside the measured process without linking anything new, writes to its own file so stdout and stderr stay byte-identical to the uninstrumented build, and disappears entirely under -DBENCH_PHASES=0 so the instrumentation's own cost can be measured as a paired result.
fork_deviations.subject: instrumentation: emit phase boundaries through bench_timer.h

fork_deviations.rationale: The ten forks must emit their phase traces through one identical header, otherwise a difference in the tracer itself becomes a difference in the numbers it produces. Keeping the copies identical is what makes the overhead measured once in the pilot valid for every method.
fork_deviations.subject: instrumentation: allow a phase span to be closed before its scope ends
fork_deviations.upstream_ref: none (file added by this fork; see its instrumentation commit)

R-EXP-11 (debug artefact output off) needs no action for this method: it writes no debug artefacts. The harness must NOT pass --no-debug-output to it -- the binary has no such flag.
